reviews.text: Cut a hole for your head to wear it as a silly hat.
Stack several to build a sturdy fort for kids.
Flatten it into a makeshift sled for sliding down grass.
reviews.failureMode: Cardboard becomes soggy and tears on damp grass, and lacks the low-friction base needed to slide.

reviews.text: Poke holes and fill with soil to grow seedlings.
reviews.failureMode: Cardboard decomposes and loses structural integrity when wet, so seedlings outgrow the collapsing box before harvest.

reviews.text: Tape it shut and use as a lightweight shipping container.
reviews.failureMode: Cardboard lacks the burst strength and water resistance required for real shipping, so it crushes under stacking loads.

reviews.text: Draw a target on it for safe indoor archery practice.
reviews.failureMode: Arrows penetrate or pass through thin cardboard, so it fails to stop projectiles safely.

reviews.text: Cut windows and doors to make a dollhouse.
Fold it into a tray for painting or messy crafts.
reviews.failureMode: Paint and moisture soak through and warp the cardboard, so it loses shape as a tray.

reviews.text: Place it over your head as a cheap eclipse viewer.
reviews.failureMode: Cardboard is not optically safe for solar viewing and transmits no filtered image, risking eye damage.

reviews.text: Stuff with clothes to make a DIY punching bag.
reviews.failureMode: Cardboard seams split and the box deforms under repeated punching impact.

reviews.text: Use as a canvas for a large painting or mural.
Cut into strips to make biodegradable packing material.
reviews.failureMode: Shredded cardboard strips lack the cushioning resilience of commercial packing material and mat down under load.
